facts.text: Dominique Jean Larrey was the chief military doctor of Napoleon's army.
Before Larrey's system, wounded soldiers were left where they fell and were gathered only after the battle ended, so their treatment was delayed by hours or even days.
In 1797 Larrey built light horse-drawn carts, called flying ambulances, with two or four wheels to rescue wounded soldiers.
In Larrey's system the injured were treated on the battlefield and then carried away in horse-drawn wagons to aid stations and hospitals.
Larrey's flying ambulances cared for soldiers on both sides of a battle.
Medical experience from the US Civil War led to the first civilian city ambulance services, in cities such as Cincinnati, New York, London and Paris.
In 1869 Edward Dalton, a former Union Army surgeon working for New York City's Board of Health, set up a city ambulance program.
Dalton's ambulances carried splints, bandages, a stomach pump and a chest of medicines.
By around 1900, young hospital doctors (interns) rode with New York's ambulances, but the ambulance drivers had almost no medical training.
In the years before World War I, carriages powered by electricity, steam and gasoline were used as ambulances.
After World War II, many US ambulances were poorly equipped hearses, and about half were run by funeral homes whose workers had usually never taken a first-aid course.
A 1966 US report called Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society found that emergency care for the injured was badly inadequate.
The US Highway Safety Act of 1966 paid for the training of emergency medical technicians (EMTs).
Taiwan's fire departments sent out ambulances 720,797 times in 2007 and 1,117,523 times in 2016.
In 2017, ambulances of Taiwan's fire departments took 5.99 minutes on average to reach the scene after a call.
Taiwan's fire agencies send ambulances through the 119 command and dispatch system.
Taiwan's rules divide emergency medical technicians into three levels: basic, intermediate and advanced.
Taiwan's fire departments use two kinds of ambulances: general ambulances and advanced life-support ambulances that must carry extra equipment.
Each ambulance team in a Taiwan fire department must have at least one ambulance and seven emergency workers.
